summary: The normalized exponential distribution on a cylindrical (vr, vx) velocity mesh before any moment compensation: one temperature per axial shift, the molecule-count factor in the exponent, the saved source's strict-interior -80 clamp, and normalization by the caller-supplied cylindrical cell volumes. Composes with the cylindrical velocity quadrature upstream and documents the seed stage that precedes the saved source's moment-compensation loop.

identity.relation: the normalized exponential seed of the saved create_shifted_maxwellian relation on a cylindrical velocity mesh, before moment compensation
identity.direction: vr, vx, normalization temperature, axial shifts in m/s, per-shift temperatures, mass, molecule count and cell volumes -> per-shift normalized distribution, thermal speed and raw exponent
identity.definition: With vth = sqrt(2 e T_norm / (m amu)), the raw exponent is -(vr^2 + (vx - shift/vth)^2) * molecule_count * T_norm / T_shift per shift. The raw seed is exp(argument) where -80 < argument < 0 and exp(-80) everywhere else -- a strict interior clamp under which a mesh node exactly at the shifted peak (argument == 0) is floored like the far tail while the returned exponent still reports the raw value. The distribution is normalized per shift by the supplied cell volumes: sum(volume * distribution) = 1 per shift.
identity.model: discretized shifted Maxwellian exponential seed on an explicit mesh; the saved source's downstream moment-compensation loop is deliberately outside this leaf
identity.geometry: velocity space, cylindrical: radial speed vr and axial velocity vx; the axial shift is applied to the vx axis
identity.coordinates: vr and vx in the caller's normalized velocity unit; shifts in m/s are divided by the thermal speed into mesh units
identity.boundary: argument == 0 is floored to exp(-80) like the far tail (strict interior clamp); the distribution is never exactly zero; molecule_count must be exactly 1 or 2; every accepted call returns finite distributions
assumptions: The cell volumes are the caller's; the cylindrical velocity quadrature produces exactly the measure this normalization consumes.
The seed is the pre-compensation stage: a caller that needs the saved source's moment-compensated distribution must not treat this seed as final.
The constants AMU_KG = 1.6726231e-27 kg and ELEMENTARY_CHARGE_C = 1.602177e-19 C are the saved source's frozen values, kept bit-compatible for replay; they are not the current CODATA estimates.
molecule_count is a saved-source convention: the exponent carries a factor 2 for molecular hydrogen relative to atomic hydrogen.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.description: Normalized axial-velocity mesh; the shift is applied to this axis.

inputs.name: tnorm_ev
inputs.description: Normalization temperature fixing the thermal speed that converts shifts into mesh units.

inputs.name: shifted_vx_m_s
inputs.description: Axial shifts of the Maxwellian peaks, one per layer.

inputs.name: temperature_ev
inputs.description: Per-shift temperatures, same length as the shifts.
inputs.constraints: A finite one-dimensional array with strictly positive entries and the shifts' shape.

inputs.name: mass_amu
inputs.description: Species mass fixing the thermal speed.

inputs.name: molecule_count
inputs.description: Molecule-count factor of the exponent: 1 for atomic, 2 for molecular hydrogen.

inputs.name: cylindrical_volume
inputs.description: Cell volumes of the cylindrical velocity mesh, rows matched to vr and columns to vx.

outputs.name: distribution
outputs.description: The normalized exponential seed, one layer per shift.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; sum(volume * distribution) = 1 per shift.

outputs.name: thermal_speed_m_s
outputs.description: The thermal speed sqrt(2 e T_norm / (m amu)) used to convert the shifts.

outputs.name: exponent
outputs.description: The raw (unclamped) exponent per mesh node and shift.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonpositive for accepted input; a zero entry marks a mesh node exactly at the shifted peak, which the seed floors to exp(-80).

preconditions: The caller supplies a consistent velocity mesh and the cylindrical cell-volume measure, in the source's N1 convention.
The caller understands the seed is the pre-compensation stage of the saved chain and does not treat it as a moment-compensated distribution.
supported: Per-shift Maxwellian seeds on an explicit cylindrical mesh with per-shift temperatures, for molecule_count 1 or 2.
The far-shift limit where every exponent sits below the -80 floor: the normalized seed becomes exactly the uniform distribution over the mesh.
Composition with the cylindrical velocity quadrature upstream and with the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average on the same mesh snapshot.
excluded: The saved source's downstream moment-compensation loop: this leaf returns the seed before compensation.
Non-Maxwellian or non-exponential seeds, and any collision or field model.
Mesh or volume generation: both are caller inputs.
Unit conversion between mesh units and m/s beyond the shift division by the thermal speed.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when vr/vx/shift/temperature/volume shapes are inconsistent or arrays are empty, when tnorm_ev or mass_amu is not a finite positive scalar, when molecule_count is not exactly 1 or 2, when a temperature is nonpositive, or when any input value is non-finite or a volume is nonpositive.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the thermal speed, the raw exponent or the normalized distribution is not representable in double precision for finite inputs that satisfy the stated domain -- for example a normalization temperature at 1e308 whose thermal speed overflows, a tiny normalization temperature with a huge shift whose quotient overflows to an infinite exponent, a 1e-320 cell volume whose normalization denominator underflows so the divided distribution overflows to infinity, or cell volumes near the float64 ceiling whose weighted raw seed sums overflow so the divided distribution collapses to exact zeros. Every accepted call then returns finite strictly-positive distributions with a unit volume-weighted sum by construction of the clamp and the checked normalization. There is no iteration and no callback.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iteration. The saved source's moment-compensation loop is outside this leaf.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no outputs.

python.signature: build_shifted_maxwellian_seed(*, vr, vx, tnorm_ev, shifted_vx_m_s, temperature_ev, mass_amu, molecule_count, cylindrical_volume)

example.description: Build the seed for one shift on a small mesh, verify the volume-weighted normalization and the strict-interior clamp witness, and compose the quadrature, the seed and the Maxwellian rate average on one mesh snapshot.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import build_shifted_maxwellian_seed, make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature
from scirel.collisions import average_cross_section_over_maxwellian

vr = np.array([0.5, 1.5])
vx = np.array([-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5])
quadrature = make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature(vr=vr, vx=vx)
volume = quadrature['volume']
seed = build_shifted_maxwellian_seed(
    vr=vr, vx=vx, tnorm_ev=20.0,
    shifted_vx_m_s=np.array([0.0]),
    temperature_ev=np.array([10.0]),
    mass_amu=2.0, molecule_count=1,
    cylindrical_volume=volume,
)
assert seed['distribution'].shape == (2, 4, 1)
assert np.sum(volume * seed['distribution'][:, :, 0]) == 1.0
assert np.all(np.isfinite(seed['distribution']))
rate = average_cross_section_over_maxwellian(
    particle_energy_ev=np.array([0.0, 10.0]),
    particle_mass_amu=1.0,
    target_temperature_ev=10.0,
    target_mass_amu=2.0,
    vx=vx, vr=vr, tnorm_ev=20.0,
    cylindrical_volume=volume,
    cross_section_m2=lambda energy: np.full_like(energy, 3.0e-20),
)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(rate)) and np.all(rate > 0.0)
try:
    build_shifted_maxwellian_seed(
        vr=vr, vx=vx, tnorm_ev=20.0,
        shifted_vx_m_s=np.array([0.0]),
        temperature_ev=np.array([10.0]),
        mass_amu=2.0, molecule_count=3,
        cylindrical_volume=volume,
    )
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'physical' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('molecule_count 3 must be rejected')
example.expected: The seed distribution has shape (2, 4, 1) with a volume-weighted sum of exactly 1 over the mesh, finite everywhere; the same mesh snapshot's quadrature volumes also feed the Maxwellian rate average to finite positive rates; and molecule_count 3 raises ValueError naming the physical-input contract.

scope: That the public callable reproduces the saved seed relation exactly: distribution, exponent and thermal speed compared against an in-file loop-per-shift formulation of the same discrete relation at rtol 1e-15.
Volume-weighted normalization: sum(volume * distribution) = 1 per shift for the supplied cell volumes.
The strict-interior clamp witness: a mesh node exactly at the shifted peak (argument == 0) is floored to exp(-80) in the distribution while the exponent output reports the raw zero.
The far-shift limit: when every exponent sits below the -80 floor, the normalized seed is exactly the uniform distribution over the mesh.
The molecule-count factor: molecule_count 2 doubles the exponent and the distribution matches the independent formulation at molecule_count 2 with unit normalization.
A positive shift moves the volume-weighted axial moment positive.
The composition contract: the cylindrical quadrature's volumes normalize the seed and feed the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average on one immutable mesh snapshot.

Output representability: a normalization temperature at 1e308 (thermal-speed overflow), a tiny normalization temperature with a 1e308 shift (infinite raw exponent), a 1e-320 cell volume (normalization denominator underflows, divided distribution overflows) and cell volumes near the float64 ceiling (weighted raw seed sums overflow, divided distribution collapses to zeros) are each rejected with a ValueError. Ordinary inputs produce unchanged numbers.
The input contract: shape consistency, finite values, positive temperatures/masses/tnorm, molecule_count exactly 1 or 2, strictly positive volumes; every out-of-domain value is rejected.
